A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from AnyMaker to CustAny. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original customization experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, ablations in Tables 2–4, and qualitative results throughout the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V4 retains the original quantitative experiments and ablations and reports additional qualitative customization outputs, including prompt variation, identity mixing, and virtual try-on examples.

M1.justification: The documented training formulation changes: Eqs. (8)–(9) assign the masked feature to the decoupling branch instead of the normal branch, and Eq. (10) changes negative cosine similarity to positive cosine similarity. The extractor and dual-level injection architecture remain unchanged. These localized corrections do not establish that the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: MC-IDC and the three quantitative evaluation domains remain unchanged. Qualitative coverage narrows slightly: v1's explicit galaxy/scenery customization demonstration in Fig. A1 disappears. Painting, sticker generation, identity mixing, and story generation remain represented after matching relocated and expanded figures.

E2.justification: The comparator sets match: IP-Adapter for general objects; IP-Adapter, PhotoMaker, and InstantID for human customization; and IP-Adapter and MagicClothing for virtual try-on. InstantID is labeled InstanceID in both Table 1 versions. The corresponding qualitative comparison also retains its comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both retain the 1,000-sample evaluation with a 4:3:3 domain split, the same metrics and diversity prompts, and the same stated training budget and inference settings. V4's encoder variants and loss coefficients specify previously omitted details; they do not establish changes to earlier settings.

E4.justification: V4 expands qualitative case studies of changing prompts with fixed references in Fig. 5 and mismatched text/image categories in Fig. 8. The extraction, injection, and decoupling ablations retain their numerical results and visual examples. The story and dog-diversity demonstrations are largely redisplayed existing evidence.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical DiverSim uncertainty entries and the same reporting practice. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an explanation of the reported plus/minus quantities.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–4 is unchanged, including the proposed method's general-object FID of 47.09 and CLIP-i of 82.16. Changes concern qualitative outputs: v4 adds prompt-variation, hybrid-identity, and garment examples and removes some v1 gallery examples. These do not demonstrate a quantitative performance improvement.

T1.justification: Eqs. (8)–(10) receive substantive corrections to their formal loss definitions: branch conditioning is reassigned and the cosine-similarity sign is reversed. These are mathematical changes rather than equivalent notation. The remaining mathematical framework is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V4 explicitly presents a novel dataset-construction pipeline as a main contribution, whereas v1 primarily claims creation of MC-IDC alongside the customization framework. The central claims about zero-shot single-reference customization, identity fidelity, text editability, and performance against specialized methods remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly explains the applicability condition for text-image identity mixing: different categories in the prompt and reference can merge into a new identity. V1 names and illustrates this application without that explicit explanation. The interpretations of encoder complementarity and decoupling remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 specifies loss weights of 2.0, 1.0, and 0.5 and names MAE-ViT-h/14 and DINOv2-ViT-g/14-reg4. Conversely, it omits v1's 0.1 conditioning-dropout rate and explicit statement that evaluation samples were randomly selected from MC-IDC. Both still describe code and dataset release as forthcoming.

R1.justification: V4 removes the Textual Inversion and ConsistentID discussions and citations. It also softens the related-work assertion that general zero-shot customization has never been studied to describing it as largely unexplored. Most cited works and the underlying research positioning remain the same.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and renamed, and the abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method passages are rewritten. The dataset section moves before the method, experimental subsections are reorganized, an applications subsection is introduced, and the appendix becomes separately headed supplementary material.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column layout, recomposes the opening teaser, adds an MC-IDC sample illustration, and redraws the architecture diagram. Tables and application figures are extensively rearranged, with expanded qualitative panels and smaller ablation displays. Existing story and dog-diversity images are reused within the new layouts.

improvement.justification: The corrected branch equations and contrastive-loss sign reduce concrete inconsistencies in v1, while newly specified loss weights and encoder variants improve reproducibility. The dataset illustration and expanded qualitative cases improve explanation. These benefits are tempered by omitted dropout and sampling details and smaller ablation panels; the quantitative evidence remains unchanged.
